_about: Glauka's passport: one stamp per main building. Walking onto the doorstep of an unstamped building brings its host out; the host greets, points out one feature you can find for real (with a close-up in a bubble), then the story's comic plays. The stamp is the badge of the headline story. gift = a wardrobe item given and worn at once.

stamps.name: Propylaia
stamps.hello: Welcome to my gateway! I had it built, and it cost a fortune.
stamps.feature: Look at the middle passage: no steps, just a ramp. That was for the cows and sheep being led up to Athena.

stamps.name: Temple of Athena Nike
stamps.hello: I am Nike, Victory. This little temple is mine.
stamps.feature: Find me in the Acropolis Museum, bending down to undo my sandal. My dress is marble, but it looks wet and thin as silk.

stamps.name: Parthenon
stamps.hello: I am Phidias. I made the giant gold and ivory Athena who stood inside.
stamps.feature: There is not one straight line in this temple. The floor bulges up in the middle, and the columns lean inwards. Make them taller and they would meet in the sky.

stamps.name: Erechtheion
stamps.hello: Psst. Down here. We six hold up this porch roof on our heads.
stamps.feature: Look at the back of our heads: one thick plait each. It makes our necks strong enough to carry the roof.

stamps.name: Theatre of Dionysus
stamps.hello: My theatre! Plays were invented right here, in my honour.
stamps.feature: See the marble thrones in the front row? The best one, in the middle, was my priest's. It has lion's paws for feet.

stamps.name: Odeon of Herodes Atticus
stamps.hello: Concerts still happen here, nearly two thousand years later.
stamps.feature: Count the rows of round arches in the big wall. Greeks hardly used arches. The Romans loved them, and this was built in Roman times.

stamps.name: Areopagus
stamps.hello: Careful up here. I once gave a speech on this rock.
stamps.feature: Feel the rock under your feet: polished like glass by millions of shoes. Look for the old steps cut into the rock beside the metal stairs.

stamps.name: Ancient Agora
stamps.hello: Ah, a new person to ask questions. Wonderful.
stamps.feature: Find the little stone by the path with letters on it. It says: I am the boundary of the Agora. It is still standing where they put it.

stamps.name: Temple of Hephaestus
stamps.hello: My temple, the best-kept in all Greece. It still has its roof.
stamps.feature: Look above the columns at the front: small carved squares. They show Heracles doing his labours, and Theseus fighting.

stamps.name: Pnyx
stamps.hello: This hill is where the people of Athens voted.
stamps.feature: Find the speaker's platform cut out of the rock, with steps up to it. Any citizen could climb up and speak.

stamps.name: Tower of the Winds
stamps.hello: I am Marcus Aurelius, emperor. Even emperors check the weather.
stamps.feature: Walk around the top of the tower: eight winds carved in stone, one on each side. Boreas, the cold north wind, wears a thick cloak.

stamps.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
stamps.hello: MY temple. The biggest in Greece. Bow, small mortal.
stamps.feature: Only a few of my columns still stand. One blew down in a storm in 1852. It still lies there, its pieces spread out like fallen coins.

stamps.name: Plato's Academy
stamps.hello: My school stood in this olive grove for hundreds of years.
stamps.feature: Athena's sacred olive trees grew here. Their oil filled the painted prize jars for the winners of her games.

stamps.name: Aristotle's Lyceum
stamps.hello: Keep up! I teach while I walk.
stamps.feature: See the square yard with rooms around it? That was the wrestling school. My students exercised and argued in the same place.

stamps.name: Parliament guards
stamps.feature: Look at my shoes. Each one has sixty nails in the sole and a big pompom on the toe. They clack on the stone when we march.
